t.E200.agn: In 2019 EFSA set a combined acceptable daily intake (ADI) for sorbic acid and potassium sorbate of 11 mg/kg body weight, expressed as sorbic acid; this value replaced the temporary limit from 2015 (3 mg/kg).
t.E200.body: In the body, sorbic acid is broken down (oxidised) in a similar way to other fatty acids such as caproic acid and is used as a source of energy.
t.E200.prod: Sorbic acid and its salts are produced by chemical synthesis; sorbic acid also occurs naturally in rowan berries.
t.E200.regx.0: Re-evaluated; combined ADI 11 mg/kg (as sorbic acid).
t.E200.summary: A preservative found naturally in rowan berries and now synthesised. Effective against moulds and yeasts; used in cheese, wine, bakery wares and sauces.
t.E200.what: Extends shelf life by slowing the growth of moulds and yeasts.
